claims.text: Partial Co doping of La(Fe,Si)13-based compounds will enhance their magnetocaloric properties.
Partial Co doping shifts the Curie temperature toward a desired operational range.
Shifting the Curie temperature toward the operational range increases the magnetic entropy change under moderate fields.
The initial material is undoped La(Fe,Si)13 prepared by standard metallurgical methods such as induction melting.
Fe is partially substituted with Co.
Partial substitution of Fe with Co tunes the Curie temperature.
Magnetocaloric performance is to be evaluated near 300 K under magnetic fields of 1–2 T.
Co substitution modifies the lattice parameter within the La(Fe,Si)13 crystal structure.
Co substitution modifies exchange interactions within the La(Fe,Si)13 crystal structure.
Co doping redistributes electronic and magnetic interactions in the lattice.
The altered electronic and magnetic interactions raise the Curie temperature.
Raising the Curie temperature aligns the peak magnetocaloric response with the targeted operational temperature.
Co-doped material will exhibit a larger isothermal magnetic entropy change in the magnetic-refrigeration temperature window than undoped La(Fe,Si)13.
The magnetocaloric response of undoped La(Fe,Si)13 typically peaks below room temperature.
Undoped La(Fe,Si)13 has a lower magnetic entropy change than the proposed Co-doped material.
Excessive Co substitution may form secondary phases.
Excessive Co substitution may degrade structural integrity and limit magnetocaloric gains.
The magnitude of enhancement depends on Co concentration and processing conditions.
A 0–10 at% Co-doping series can be compared with undoped La(Fe,Si)13 using Curie-temperature, entropy-change, and X-ray-diffraction measurements.
The hypothesis is falsified if Co doping neither shifts the Curie temperature nor increases the magnetocaloric effect under moderate fields relative to the undoped control.
